subject: Request: Customer exception for uptime floor and latency carveout
messages:
From: Leland Thompson <leland@novexhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA bounds for pilot (uptime floor / latency carveout)

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re excited to move the pilot into production for a small cohort (100k monthly requests) but we need to confirm three things before procurement will greenlight the PO:

1) Uptime floor — our procurement team is asking if you can accept a 99.7% uptime floor for the pilot (we can’t commit to 99.9% until after real traffic patterns).
2) Latency SLO — due to how our integration batches requests, we need a temporary 95th p95 latency target of 120ms for the pilot rather than the standard 50ms.
3) Credit cap and discount — if you accept both exceptions, procurement is pushing for a 20% first-year discount and a cap on service credits to three months of fees.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to accommodate those concessions for a 3-month pilot? We can sign an amendment and start with a pilot clause.

Thanks,
Leland Thompson
Director of Platform Engineering
Novex Health

---
Attachments: novex-sla-exception-request.pdf (PDF, 190KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Leland Thompson <leland@novexhealth.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@novexhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA bounds for pilot (uptime floor / latency carveout)

Hi Leland —

Appreciate the clarity and the pilot timeline. I’ll coordinate internally and confirm the set of approvals we need. Short answer: we can consider a temporary uptime floor and latency carveout for a limited pilot, but approvals are required for commercial concessions (discount + credit cap).

I’m copying Avery (Head of Revenue), Jonas (Deal Desk / Legal), and Sean (VP Operations) to request a quick decision and list the proposed guardrails I think we should attach to any exception: 

- Pilot length: 3 months with a mandatory 30-day performance review.
- Credit cap: not to exceed 3 months of gross monthly fees for the pilot period.
- Discount: prelim request of 20% first-year (or equivalent pilot credit) to be finalized by deal desk.
- Observability & runbook: Novex must provide traffic pattern samples + oncall contacts; Redwood asks for instrumentation access and a joint runbook.
- Phased rollout: production traffic capped at 100k requests/month for the pilot.

I’ve attached the customer's PDF and an internal workbook (customer-prod-sla-request.xlsx) with numbers. Will circle back after internal responses.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Request: SLA bounds for pilot (uptime floor / latency carveout)

Team —

I reviewed Novex’s request and redlined a couple of legal/contract concerns in the attached proposed-amendment-draft.docx. High-level notes: 

- We can provision a temporary uptime floor of 99.7% for a defined pilot window with an explicit re-evaluation clause.
- For latency, we should accept a p95 = 120ms carveout only if Novex provides representative traffic traces and agrees to a phased ramp.
- Credit cap to three months is acceptable provided we require a performance remediation plan and that credits are the sole remedy (no termination for pilot period solely on latency misses).
- The 20% discount is negotiable; suggest offering an equivalent onboarding credit up-front instead of a list-price reduction to preserve standard renewal economics.

I recommend we require the following operational controls before sign-off:
1) Access to request-level sampling for 30 days pre-go-live.
2) A joint runbook and escalation path documented in Confluence.
3) A pilot exit criteria doc (metrics + timeline) — we can use the 30-day review to decide on full production SLOs.

If Sean is comfortable with operational mitigations, I’m OK authorizing Deal Desk to proceed with a conditional amendment and the onboarding credit alternative.

Jonas
Director, Deal Desk & Legal
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA bounds for pilot (uptime floor / latency carveout)

Marissa / Jonas —

I’m comfortable granting an operational exception for a 3-month pilot with the following conditions (Ops exec clearance CODE: OPS-EX-22):

- Uptime floor: 99.7% for pilot window (explicit start/end dates)
- Latency carveout: p95 = 120ms for pilot only with phased ramp and sampling verification
- Credit cap: maximum of 3 months fees; credits only, no termination rights tied to pilot SLOs
- Instrumentation: Novex provides request traces + oncall contacts; Redwood gets read-only access to one observability dashboard.
- Financial commitment: 10% prepayment of pilot fees as commitment; onboarding credit (equal to 15% of pilot fees) applied up-front in lieu of a list-price discount.

Operational requirements: we need the joint runbook, a mitigation playbook, and a scheduled 30-day review meeting with Novex engineers and Redwood SREs. Legal and Deal Desk should finalize the amendment language. I authorize Deal Desk to sign off on the amendment once these conditions are documented and Novex agrees.

Sean Gallagher
VP, Product Operations — Redwood Inference
